findings.title: On phone the building tools are off-screen, yet the tips send the player to them
findings.detail: On a 390 px phone the bottom toolbar shows only the 7 road icons, the grid and half a roundabout. Houses, shop, office, upgrade, bulldoze and undo sit past the right edge, and the only hint is a soft fade. On the next screen the tip says 'Choose a building in the toolbar', but no building is visible, so a new player is stuck at the second step. Same on city, drawing-road, building-panel, signal-panel, saves and level-up phone shots.
findings.fix: On phone, collapse the 7 road types into one road button with a pop-up picker (or two rows), so the building group always shows. At minimum, scroll the toolbar to the building group when the 'Place your buildings' tip appears, and show a clear scroll arrow.
findings.evidence: fresh-city@phone.dom.json lists toolbar controls only up to 'Roundabout (O)' at [360,791,40,40]. 'Junctions', the three building kinds, 'Bulldozer', 'Undo' and 'Redo' are missing from the visible controls. city@phone tip reads 'Place your buildings. Choose a building in the toolbar and click beside a street.'

findings.title: The tip says to pick a building from the toolbar, but no building tool is on screen
findings.detail: On a phone the toolbar scrolls sideways, and the first nine visible slots are all road tools. The tip in the top right reads 'Choose a building in the toolbar', yet the building tools are off-screen to the right, and the only hint is a 28px fade over a half-cut roundabout icon. A new player looks at the toolbar, sees only roads and gets stuck on the step that unlocks the rest of the level. (New rule idea: on small screens, every tool a tip refers to must be visible when the tip shows.)
findings.fix: On phones, scroll the toolbar to the buildings group whenever the active tip mentions buildings (group.scrollIntoView({inline:'start'})). Add a visible 44px '›' scroll button in place of the mask-only fade, or split the toolbar into Roads / Buildings / Tools tabs below 720px.
findings.evidence: city@phone.dom.json controls stop at 'Roundabout (O)' [360,791,40,40], which runs past the 390px viewport. No building tool is in the visible controls, while desktop shows them at x 787-905. The tutorial text reads "Place your buildings. Choose a building in the toolbar and click beside a street." hud.css .toolbar.more-r mask fades only the last 28px. · Visible controls end at 'Roundabout (O)' [360,791,40,40], which runs past the 390 px viewport. No building control is listed in city@phone.dom.json. The tip text is 'Place your buildings. Choose a building in the toolbar and click beside a street.' · city@phone.dom.json: the last visible control is 'Roundabout (O)' at [360,791,40,40], which is already cut by the 390 px edge. 'Small Commercial', 'Small Office', the house button, bulldozer and undo have no box on screen. Tip text: 'Place your buildings. Choose a building in the toolbar and click beside a street.' · Toolbar tools [13-400,791,h40] end at y=831 (844-831 = 13 px, need 34); Game menu [8,8,30,26] top at 8 px (need 47).
alsoNoted: hierarchy: Tip says to pick a building, but no building tool is on screen
hud: On phone the house, shop and office buttons are off-screen while the tip asks the player to use them
rules: HUD hugs the screen edges, inside the notch and home-bar zones

findings.title: Tip points to building tools that are not on screen, and says 'click' on a touch device
findings.detail: The tip tells the player to 'Choose a building in the toolbar and click beside a street', but on phone the toolbar is cut off after the grid tool and the house/shop/office buttons are off-screen to the right, with only a faint fade as a scroll cue. A new phone player cannot find the control the tip names. Same on fresh-city, drawing-road, overlay-flow, building-panel, signal-panel and saves at phone width.
findings.fix: On phone, put buildings in view (e.g. a second toolbar row or a Roads/Buildings switch), or auto-scroll the toolbar to the buildings group when this tip shows; switch tip verbs to 'tap' on touch input.
findings.evidence: Phone toolbar controls end at Roundabout [360,791,40,40], which already overflows the 390 px viewport; no building button appears in the phone DOM controls. Tip text: 'Place your buildings. Choose a building in the toolbar and click beside a street.' Fresh-city tip also says 'click to start and click again to finish'.

findings.title: Elevation level numbers 0-3 are close to invisible: white text on pastel fills
findings.detail: While drawing a road, the player picks the deck level from four buttons whose only readable mark is a white digit on a light cyan, green, blue or lilac fill. The three unselected buttons are also faded to 55% opacity, so the digits almost disappear and the colour is left as the only cue. Players who don't distinguish those colours can't tell levels 1, 2 and 3 apart when they build bridges. Same buttons on drawing-road@phone (identical ratios).
findings.fix: Make each level button white (#fff) with #26282c digits (about 15:1) and mark its level with a 4px bottom bar in the level colour (border-bottom:4px solid #58c8e6 / #74b83e / #4f8fe8 / #9a6ae0). Drop opacity:0.55, mark the selected level with the existing 2px ring plus a #d5eefa fill, and raise the buttons to at least 28x28.
findings.evidence: contrast.md drawing-road@desktop: "0" 1.94:1, "1" 1.66:1, "2" 2.00:1, "3" 2.21:1 declared (p10 1.01) at 12px against a 4.5:1 requirement. hud.css .seg-btn.lvl { color:#fff; opacity:0.55 } on .lvl0 #58c8e6, .lvl1 #74b83e, .lvl2 #4f8fe8, .lvl3 #9a6ae0. Buttons are 24x24. · contrast.md drawing-road@desktop: '1' 1.66:1, '2' 2.0:1, '3' 2.21:1, '0' 1.94:1 (white, 12 px). The chips are 24x24 at about [798,803,104,27]. drawing-road@phone gives the same values. · '1','2','3' white on (116,184,62) / (79,143,232) / (154,106,224) with opacity 0.55: 1.66 / 2.00 / 2.21 declared, p10 1.01; rule needs 4.5:1.
alsoNoted: hud: Elevation level numbers are white on pastel chips and can't be read
rules: Elevation level numbers 1-3 are nearly invisible

findings.title: Overlays menu on phone opens underneath the money/speed bar and the tip card
findings.detail: New idea: a dropdown must layer above every other HUD element. Opening Overlays on phone, the selected 'Traffic flow' row is hidden behind the $ chip and speed buttons, and the right half of the first three rows is cut off by the purple tip, so the player can't read or tap the options they came for.
findings.fix: Give the overlays menu a z-index above the HUD chips and tip, or open it as a bottom sheet on phone. Hide the tip while a menu is open.
findings.evidence: Menu rows start at y=47 ('Traffic flow' [13,47,226,25]), and the money chip [18,50,45,15] plus speed buttons (y 45-69) draw over them. The tip card (x 192-381, y 44-141) cuts 'Overall building satisfacti', 'Access to nearby commer', 'Access to nearby workpla'. · Menu items span x 13-239, y 47-247 (dom). Money chip [18,50,45,15] and speed buttons [80-186,45,24] sit on the 'Traffic flow' row at y 47-72. The tip card (x>=192, y 44-142) truncates the visible labels to 'Overall building satisfacti', 'Access to nearby commer' and 'Access to nearby workpla'.
alsoNoted: hierarchy: Overlays menu opens underneath the money chip, speed control and tip card

findings.title: On phone the Overlays menu opens underneath the money, speed controls and tip card
findings.detail: NEW: a dropdown opened from the HUD must stack above the other HUD panels. On phone the overlay list drops into the second HUD row, so the money pill and pause/speed bar cover its first item ('Traffic flow'), and the purple tip card cuts off the right half of the next three items ('Overall building satisfacti', 'Access to nearby commer', 'Access to nearby workpla'). The player can't read, or reliably tap, the overlay they just chose.
findings.fix: Give the overlay dropdown a higher z-index than the money/speed bar and the tip card, and hide the tip while a HUD menu is open. Better still, on phone open it as a full-width sheet under the top row.
findings.evidence: overlay-flow@phone.dom.json: menu items run from [13,47,226,25] to [13,222,226,25]. Money is at [18,50,45,15], the speed buttons at [80..186,45,24], and the tip text box starts at x=203, y=53. In the screenshot, 'Traffic flow' is hidden behind '$13,960' and the pause/play buttons. · Menu rows start at [13,47,226,25] while '$13,960' [18,50,45,15] and the speed buttons [80-186,45,h24] draw on top of it; screenshot shows 'Overall building satisfacti', 'Access to nearby commer', 'Access to nearby workpla' cut by the tip card (x ~193). Measured p10 contrast 3.04 on the first two rows.
alsoNoted: rules: Open Overlays menu is buried under the money chip, speed buttons and tip card

findings.title: Traffic-light editor controls are 14-20 px touch targets packed 2 px apart
findings.detail: On a phone, each phase row puts W/E/S approach toggles, the shorter and longer buttons and a remove-phase X into a strip where every target is smaller than a fingertip. Tapping 'E' easily toggles 'W' or 'S', and tapping '+' can hit the delete X right next to it, which removes the whole phase.
findings.fix: Under @media (pointer: coarse), make .arm, .dur and .ph-del at least 44x44 with 8px gaps. Split each phase onto two lines: name and duration stepper on top, approach toggles below. Move the remove-phase X to the row's far left, or put it behind a long-press, so it can't sit next to '+'.
findings.evidence: signal-panel@phone.dom.json: W 20x17, E 16x17, S 16x17 at x 83/105/123 (2px gaps); minus 18x18; plus 18x18 at x 327; Remove phase 16x14 at x 349 (4px from plus). All are under the 44x44 phone minimum. Desktop has the same sizes (contrast.md lists 26 small targets). · dom: W [83,634,20,17], E [105,634,16,17], S [123,634,16,17] (2 px gaps); '-' [284,633,18,18]; '+' [327,633,18,18]; Remove phase [349,635,16,14]. Rule needs 44x44 on touch with 8 px spacing.
alsoNoted: rules: Traffic-light phase toggles and steppers are far too small to tap

findings.title: Half the goals show as already done on an empty map
findings.detail: Before the player has built anything, the goal card reads '2/4', with green ticks on '95% building satisfaction 100.0%' and '95% traffic flow 100.0%', plus a green 'no residents' beside the trip goal. A newcomer reads this as progress they made and can't tell which goals actually need work. The trip goal label is cut off as 'Trip taken by every n…', so its meaning is lost too.
findings.fix: Show goals that can't be measured yet as neutral (grey dash, 'needs residents') instead of ticked, and count them toward n/4 only once buildings exist. Shorten the label to 'Every resident makes a trip' so it fits.
findings.evidence: 'City Level 1 2/4'. Ticked: '95% building satisfaction 100.0%', '95% traffic flow 100.0%'. 'no residents' is in good-green rgb(46,158,74). The label is truncated on screen while its full width is 189 px.

findings.title: Goal progress values are 11px in green or red that fail contrast
findings.detail: The right-hand values in the goals card ('16 to go', 'no residents', '100.0%') are the numbers a player checks to see how close the level is. They are the smallest, lowest-contrast text in the HUD, so they read as faint coloured smudges next to bolder labels. This repeats on every in-play desktop shot. The same red token makes 'Remove lights' fail at 4.33:1 in signal-panel.
findings.fix: Darken the tokens to --good:#1f7a36 (about 5.2:1 on the card) and --bad:#c0332e (about 5.4:1), and set .obj-val to 12px, weight 500. The green tick and empty circle already carry the done/not-done state, so the darker colours lose no meaning.
findings.evidence: contrast.md fresh-city@desktop: "100.0%" 3.38:1 at 11px, "no residents" 3.38:1 at 11px, "16 to go" 4.25:1 at 11px (all fail on size and contrast). building-panel "100%" in green bold 12px measures 3.38:1. hud.css --good:#2e9e4a, --bad:#d9443f, .obj-val { font-size:11px }.

findings.title: Unmet goal shows 'no residents' in success green, and its own name is truncated
findings.detail: On the very first screen the 'Trip taken by every new resident' goal has an empty circle (not met), but its status is written in the same green as the met '100.0%' goals, so it reads as fine. Its label is also cut to 'Trip taken by every n...' because the status text takes the space.
findings.fix: Show not-yet-measurable status in the neutral grey (or a dash), keep green for met only, and shorten the goal label (for example 'Every resident makes a trip') or let it wrap.
findings.evidence: 'no residents' rgb(46,158,74), the same as '100.0%' [1362,79]. The label box [1197,57,189,15] runs into the value at x 1334, and the screenshot shows 'Trip taken by every n...'. · fresh-city@desktop: goal row text 'Trip taken by every n…' next to 'no residents' [1334,57,65,14]. In city@desktop the full label 'Trip taken by every new resident' [1197,57,189,15] fits. · 'no residents' (46,158,74) beside an unchecked circle; '16 to go' (217,68,63) at game start; elsewhere green = goal met (100.0% with filled check).
alsoNoted: hud: A goal label is cut off on the first screen of a new city
rules: Goal colours contradict the checkmarks: green on an unmet goal, alarm red on normal progress

findings.title: First tip says 'pick the two-way street below' but doesn't point to it
findings.detail: The tip sends the player to the toolbar, where they find seven near-identical lane diagrams with no labels and nothing highlighted. They have to hover icons one by one to find 'Street (2)', the second icon.
findings.fix: While this tip is up, pulse or outline the Street button (and show its name above it). Mention the key in the tip: 'Pick Street (2)'.
findings.evidence: Tip: 'Draw a street. Pick the two-way street below, click to start and click again to finish.' The road group [365,849,278,38] has 7 unlabelled 38x38 icons. No pulse or outline on 'Street (2)' at [405,849,38,38]. · Tip at [1179,143,224,67]: 'Draw a street. Pick the two-way street below...'. Road tools [365-643,849,38,38] have no visible labels, and the Street (2) tool [405,849,38,38] has no highlight in fresh-city@desktop.png.
alsoNoted: hierarchy: First tip points to 'the two-way street below', but nothing in the toolbar is marked

findings.title: Building buttons are named only by a number
findings.detail: The three building tools show a house, a blue block and a purple block with small counts. Their tooltip/aria name is just that count, so hovering gives the player '14' instead of 'House'. The player can't tell which is a shop and which is an office, or that the number means 'left to place'.
findings.fix: Name each one in its tooltip and aria-label, as the road tools are: 'Small Residential (14 left) · …'. Make the count badge at least 12 px.
findings.evidence: Controls: '14' [787,849,38,38], '1' [827,849,38,38], '1' [867,849,38,38]. Badge digits are 10 px. On city@desktop the residential button is still labelled only '6'.

findings.title: On phone the level goals are collapsed out of sight
findings.detail: The phone layout shows only 'City Level 1 2/4 >'. The four goals, and which ones are missing, sit behind a chevron the player may never tap, so they don't know what levels them up.
findings.fix: Expand the goal card on first launch (and whenever a goal changes state), or show the next unmet goal as one line under the header, e.g. '16 buildings to place'.
findings.evidence: fresh-city@phone.dom.json has no goal text ('All buildings placed', '16 to go' are absent). Only 'City Level 1' and '2/4' are visible at [201,15,...]. · Only 'City Level 1' [201,15,69,15] and '2/4' [276,16,19,14] are visible. No goal rows exist in fresh-city@phone.dom.json, while the tip occupies [192,44,190,98]. · Phone goal card is only the header button [201,15,172,15] with a '>' chevron; none of the four goal labels appear in the phone DOM.
alsoNoted: hierarchy: On phone the four level goals are collapsed to 'City Level 1 2/4' and the tip takes their place
rules: On phone the level goals are collapsed to '2/4' at the start

findings.title: The tutorial tip, the main instruction text, shrinks to 11px on phones
findings.detail: The purple tip is the only place that tells a new player what to do next, and the phone layout makes it smaller than on desktop and squeezes it into a 150px column. Players have to hold the phone close to read a five-line paragraph of 11px text. The same applies to every phone shot with the tip.
findings.fix: Delete the .tutorial font-size:11px override and set it to 14px/1.4 on phones. Below 720px, move the tip out of the narrow right column to a full-width card under the top rows (left:8px; right:8px; top:80px), with the bold lead sentence on its own line.
findings.evidence: contrast.md fresh-city@phone: tip paragraph at 11px, box 203,53,150,78 (size fail; contrast 4.86:1 passes). hud.css @media (max-width:720px) { .tutorial { font-size:11px } .tr { width:min(264px, calc(100vw - 200px)) } } gives a 190px card on a 390px phone. Phone body text should be at least 14px. · Tip 'Pick the two-way street below...' [203,53,150,78] size 11; '2/4' 11 px; toolbar count '14' 10 px; contrast.md font sizes per shot: 10, 11, 12.
alsoNoted: rules: Tutorial tip and HUD text drop to 11 px on phone

findings.title: Goal card has no type hierarchy: title, goals and values are all 11-12 px
findings.detail: The whole HUD uses 10, 11 and 12 px only. In the goals card the level title, the four goal names and their values differ by at most 1 px, so the eye can't jump from 'which level' to 'what's left'. The same flatness is in the inspector ('Small Commercial' 12/600 against 'Satisfaction' 12/400) and the junction panel ('Junction' 12/600 against 'Phase 1' 12/500).
findings.fix: Keep the small flat look but add one clear step: card title about 14 px/600 with the 3/4 counter in the same size, goal labels at 12-13, and values at 12/600 in tabular figures so the status column reads first.
findings.evidence: 'City Level 1' 12 px/600, '3/4' 11/500, goal labels 12/400, '6 to go' and '100.0%' 11/400. contrast.md lists font sizes 10, 11, 12 for every in-play desktop shot.

findings.title: Goal values use alarm red for normal progress and a pale green that fails contrast
findings.detail: '6 to go' on the unmet buildings goal is shown in the alarm red, the same red as 'Remove lights' and the 'Jammed' end of the flow legend, although it is just normal progress. The met values '100.0%' are a light green that is hard to read at 11 px. On fresh-city, the unmet trip goal shows 'no residents' in that same green, so the colour no longer tells met from unmet. The four goals are the main thing the player is working towards.
findings.fix: Show progress values in the neutral dark text colour (rgb 38,40,44) and let the check/empty circle carry met/unmet. Keep red for a goal that is actually slipping (e.g. flow dropping under 95%), and darken the green to at least 4.5:1 if it stays.
findings.evidence: '6 to go' rgb(217,68,63) 11 px, 4.25:1; '100.0%' rgb(46,158,74) 11 px, 3.38:1 (contrast.md, fails 4.5:1). fresh-city@desktop: 'no residents' 3.41:1 in green next to an empty (unmet) circle.

findings.title: Goal progress values are low-contrast 11 px coloured text
findings.detail: The numbers that say whether each level goal is met ('6 to go', '100.0%') are the most important readout in the goal card but the faintest text in it. White-on-blue buttons and tags ('Continue', 'Save', the 'Commercial' tag, 3.75:1) and active W/E/S toggles (white on green, 2.33:1) fail the same rule.
findings.fix: Darken the good/bad text tokens (green to ~#1f7a3a, red to ~#b8322d) and set values at 12 px medium; darken the button blue to ~#1f6fc4 for white text.
findings.evidence: '100.0%' green (46,158,74) on #fdfdfc = 3.38:1 at 11 px; '6 to go' red (217,68,63) = 4.25:1 at 11 px; need 4.5:1. Present on every desktop shot.

findings.title: On phone the HUD sits inside the notch and home-bar zones
findings.detail: The menu, Overlays and goal card start 8 px from the top, inside the 47 px notch/status-bar zone. The build toolbar ends 8 px above the bottom edge, where the iOS home indicator sits, so a swipe across the toolbar can trigger the system home gesture. The same applies on every phone capture.
findings.fix: Pad the top HUD row with max(env(safe-area-inset-top), 12px) and the toolbar with env(safe-area-inset-bottom) plus 8 px, with viewport-fit=cover so the insets are reported.
findings.evidence: city@phone.dom.json: 'Game menu' [8,8,30,26], 'Overlays' [44,8,85,26], goal title at y=15. Toolbar buttons [13..400,791,40,40], with the toolbar plate ending at y≈836 of 844.

findings.title: On phone the goal card is always collapsed, so the player can't see which goal is unmet
findings.detail: On phone the four level goals shrink to 'City Level 1 3/4' and stay that way in every capture. The player knows one goal is missing but not which one, or that it needs '6 to go' more buildings, without tapping a 15 px tall row. On desktop the same information is always visible.
findings.fix: On phone, show the first unmet goal inline under the title (e.g. 'Place buildings · 6 to go') and make the whole card a ≥44 px tap target that expands the full list.
findings.evidence: city@phone.dom.json: only 'City Level 1' [201,15,69,15] and '3/4' [276,16,18,14] are shown. The control 'City Level 1 3/4' is 172x15. None of the goal rows ('All buildings placed', '6 to go', …) are in the phone DOM.

findings.title: Core HUD controls on phone (speed, menu, close X) are 18-30 px targets
findings.detail: The speed buttons a player taps constantly (pause, play, fast, fastest) are 26px wide and touch each other, so a tap meant for pause often lands on play or fast. The tip's close X and panel close Xs are 18x18 at the screen edge, and the goals header is a 15px-tall strip.
findings.fix: Add @media (pointer: coarse) { .speed-btn { min-width:44px; min-height:44px } .btn, .icon-btn { min-height:44px } .close, .ph-del, .mag { min-width:44px; min-height:44px } .tool { width:44px; height:44px } .obj-head { min-height:44px } }. Where the layout can't grow, add an invisible ::after hit area with inset:-10px.
findings.evidence: contrast.md city@phone small targets (need 44x44): Pause 26x24, Normal speed 26x24, Fast 26x24, Fastest 28x24 (no gaps), Game menu 30x26, Overlays 85x26, Hide tips 18x18, City Level 1 header 172x15. building-panel and saves add Close 18x18, Pick up 62x26, Delete save 28x24 next to Load. Toolbar tools are 40x40.

findings.title: Seven road types are unlabeled lane glyphs, explained only by hover tooltips
findings.detail: The road tools are near-identical lane diagrams; their names and rules ('Boulevard ... Too busy for houses') live only in tooltips, which never appear on touch, so a phone player cannot tell Highway 3 from Boulevard or learn which roads allow buildings.
findings.fix: On selection show a short name-and-rule caption above the toolbar (e.g. 'Avenue · buildings allowed'), on both touch and mouse.
findings.evidence: Controls labelled 'Avenue (4) · Two-way, two lanes each way. Buildings can still...' etc. render as 40x40 icons with no visible text; no hover on touch.

findings.title: 'Elevation 0 1 2 3' gives no clue what it does and the digits barely show
findings.detail: While drawing a road, a strip offers 'Elevation' with four coloured squares numbered 0-3. Nothing says these build bridges or overpasses, and the buttons have no tooltip. The digits 1-3 are white at 55% opacity on light green, blue and purple, so they nearly disappear. Same on drawing-road@phone.
findings.fix: Add tooltips such as 'Ground', 'Bridge level 1'..., or rename the strip to 'Height (bridges)'. Draw the digits at full opacity in dark ink on the tinted squares.
findings.evidence: Controls are named just '0','1','2','3' [799-901,804,24,24]. Text opacity 0.55. Measured contrast for '1' 1.66, '2' 2.00, '3' 2.21 (needs 4.5).

findings.title: Junction diagram and in-world signal dots show go/stop by red vs green only
findings.detail: The phase diagram draws each arm green (moves this phase) or red (waits), and the junction on the map shows the same states as plain green and red dots. For a red-green colour-blind player (about 1 in 12 men), the two arms differ only slightly in brightness, so they can't check which approach a phase releases without reading the W/E/S chips.
findings.fix: Give the states a shape as well as a colour. In the diagram, draw 'go' arms solid with an arrowhead pointing out of the junction, and 'stop' arms as a short stub ending in a perpendicular bar (or dashed). Label each arm end with W/E/S to match the chips. On the map, draw the stop dot as a square or a dot with a dark ring, and keep go as a plain circle.
findings.evidence: hud.ts diagram stroke = on ? #34c25a : plan ? #e5484d : #b6bbc1. roads3d.ts signal colours 0x34c25a / 0xf5b82e / 0xe5484d. Relative luminance is 0.40 vs 0.22 (about 1.8:1 between them), with the same shape and width. Visible in signal-panel@desktop at the T-shaped diagram and the dots at about (678,386) and (728,420). · Diagram arms: W and E green, S red, same width and shape, no label or pattern; map dots at the junction are plain green/red circles.
alsoNoted: rules: Junction diagram shows go/stop only as green vs red arms

findings.title: Traffic-light phases use W/E/S letters the junction diagram never labels
findings.detail: The editor lists 'Phase 1 W E S' and 'Phase 2 W E S' as tiny toggles, but the diagram above shows only coloured arms with no compass letters. A new player can't tell which arm 'S' is or what a 'phase' means. The toggles are 16-20 x 17 px, so they're also hard to hit.
findings.fix: Put W/E/S labels on the diagram arms, or make each phase row a mini-diagram you click. Add a one-line hint: 'Each phase is a green light for the arms you pick'. Make the toggles at least 28x28.
findings.evidence: Phase toggles 'W' [1243,370,20,17], 'E' [1265,370,16,17], 'S' [1283,370,16,17] are 10 px text. Unselected letters measure 1.07:1 over their background. The diagram has no text labels.

findings.title: Active approach letters are 10px white on light green and fail contrast
findings.detail: The W/E/S chips tell the player which approaches get green in each phase, which is the core of the light editor. The active ones put tiny white letters on a bright green fill that is hard to read, so players have to rely on fill alone to see which approaches are on. Same on signal-panel@phone.
findings.fix: Set .arm to font-size:12px, weight 600, and .arm.on to background:#1f7a36; border-color:#17602a; color:#fff (about 5.4:1). Alternatively keep #34c25a and use #10331b text. Add a check glyph or underline to the 'on' state so it doesn't depend on fill alone.
findings.evidence: contrast.md signal-panel@desktop: W, E and S on the green chip measure 2.33:1 at 10px (size fail and contrast fail). The inactive chips are #5d6168 on white, 6.22:1 but also 10px. hud.css .arm { font-size:10px } .arm.on { background:#34c25a; color:#fff }. · signal-panel@desktop.dom.json: W [1243,370,20,17], E [1265,370,16,17], S [1283,370,16,17]; text 10 px. contrast.md: active letters declared 2.33:1, measured 1.01–1.07 p10.
alsoNoted: hud: Traffic-light phase directions are 10 px letters, with white on green at 2.33:1

findings.title: Delete-save button is the same bare X as the dialog's close button
findings.detail: Next to 'Load' sits an unlabelled X that deletes the save. It looks the same as the X that closes the dialog 100 px above, so a player who wants to leave may click it and lose their city. The prefilled name 'City Level 1' next to an existing 'Riverside' save also leaves it unclear whether Save overwrites or creates a new save.
findings.fix: Use a trash icon with a 'Delete' tooltip and ask for confirmation (or offer undo). Prefill the input with the current save's name, or label the button 'Save as new'.
findings.evidence: 'Delete save' [893,454,28,24] is icon-only. 'Close' [916,358,18,18] is the same X glyph. The Save name input value is 'City Level 1'. The existing save is named 'Riverside'.

findings.title: Level-up banner never says the level is complete or what the list means
findings.detail: The banner's title is just 'City Level 2', followed by '10 × Small Residential · 1 × Copper Mine · ...' with no verb. A newcomer can't tell whether these are rewards, unlocks or the next things to place. 'Copper Works' and 'area unlock' are new terms. Meanwhile the goal card behind still reads 'City Level 1 3/4' with '6 to go' in red, which contradicts the banner.
findings.fix: Headline 'Level 1 complete!', then 'Next: place 10 houses, a copper mine, copper works and a shop', with the reward line labelled 'Reward:'. Update the goal card when the banner shows.
findings.evidence: Banner text: 'City Level 2' / '10 × Small Residential · 1 × Copper Mine · 1 × Copper Works · 1 × Small Commercial' / '+$8,000 road budget · 1 area unlock'. Goal card: 'City Level 1 3/4', 'All buildings placed 6 to go'. · 'City Level 2' 15 px/600 [677,65,87,19]. '10 x Small Residential · 1 x Copper Mine · 1 x Copper Works · 1 x Small Commercial' 12 px grey rgb(93,97,104) [485,88,471,15]. Phone wraps to [73,88,243,30]. · level-up@desktop.dom.json: 'City Level 2' [677,65,87,19]; '10 × Small Residential · 1 × Copper Mine · 1 × Copper Works · 1 × Small Commercial' [485,88,471,15]; '+$8,000 road budget · 1 area unlock' [615,105,209,15] in grey rgb(93,97,104). The goal card still shows 'City Level 1' and '3/4'.
alsoNoted: hierarchy: Level-complete banner never says the level is complete; the reward list is one grey run-on line
hud: Level-up banner never says the level is complete, and the HUD beside it still shows Level 1

findings.title: The stale purple tip card is the loudest thing on every screen, louder than goals, panels and the level banner
findings.detail: The only saturated filled block in the HUD is the tip, and it keeps showing 'Place your buildings.' in every state: while drawing a road, inspecting a shop, editing a traffic light, in the saves dialog, and here under the level-complete banner. The eye goes to old advice before the goals card or the white banner announcing the new level. On desktop it also pushes the inspector and junction panels down to y 228.
findings.fix: Calm the tip: white card with a purple left rule or purple heading, the same weight as the goals card. Auto-dismiss or advance it once its step is done, and hide it while a modal, inspector or level banner is open.
findings.evidence: Tip bg rgb(123,93,208) with white 12 px text at [1168,133,264,88], against a white #FDFDFC goal card and a white level banner. The same 'Place your buildings.' text appears in city, drawing-road, overlay-flow, building-panel, signal-panel, saves and level-up.

findings.title: Primary buttons (Continue, Save) and zone tags use white on a mid blue that fails 4.5:1
findings.detail: The one button that moves the player on after a level ('Continue'), the Save button and the 'Commercial' zone tag in the building inspector all use white text on #2f86e0. At 11-12px that is below the AA requirement, so the most important button label is also among the least crisp. The other zone tags are worse: white on residential green #4fae36 works out to about 2.8:1.
findings.fix: Use .btn.primary { background:#2373c4; border-color:#1a5fa6 } (about 4.9:1; #2373c4 is already its border colour) with a hover of #2a7fd4. Zone tags: .z-com #2373c4, .z-res #2f7d22 (about 5.2:1), .z-ind #5f646b (about 6.0:1), .z-work #6f52bd. Set .zone-tag to 12px.
findings.evidence: contrast.md: level-up "Continue" 3.75:1 declared at 12px; saves "Save" 3.75:1; building-panel "Commercial" 3.75:1 at 11px (size fail). hud.css .btn.primary { background:#2f86e0; color:#fff }, .z-com #2f86e0, .z-res #4fae36, .z-ind #7d828a (about 3.9:1).

findings.title: Level-up banner on phone overlaps the tip card and money chip, with text showing through
findings.detail: New idea: modal banners should cover or hide the HUD they overlap, never blend with it. On phone the banner sits over the purple tip and the $/speed bar. 'Place your buildings...' bleeds through behind 'City Level 2' and the reward lines, and the money reads '$13,96'.
findings.fix: Hide the tip card (and dim the HUD) while the banner shows, make the banner opaque, and place it below the top HUD rows on phone.
findings.evidence: Banner spans about x 55-334, y 52-223, and the tip card spans x 192-381, y 44-141. Measured p10 contrast drops to 1.93 for '+$8,000 road budget · 1 area unlock' and 1.08 for the tip text underneath. · Banner [55,52,280,172] covers tip text runs [203,53,138,78] and $13,960 [18,50,45,15]. The '$13,960' chip is cut to '$13,96' and the tip's purple and white text show through behind '1 x Copper Mine · 1' and 'x Copper Works'. · contrast.md level-up@phone: '+$8,000 road budget · 1 area unlock' p10 1.93:1, and 'Place your buildings.' measures 1.08:1 where the card covers it. Banner spans roughly [55,52,280,172] and overlaps money [18,50,45,15] and the speed buttons [80..186,45,24]. · '+$8,000 road budget · 1 area unlock' p10 1.93; tip text under it p10 1.08; money chip visibly clipped to '$13,96'; ghosted 'Place your buildings.' visible inside the banner.
alsoNoted: hierarchy: Level-complete banner is see-through over the tip card and HUD, so its text sits on other text
hud: On phone the level banner is see-through and overlaps the money, speed controls and tip
rules: Level-up banner overlaps the HUD and the tip text bleeds through its reward lines

findings.title: Level banner is see-through and lies on top of the tip and speed controls, with ghost text behind its lines
findings.detail: On a phone the 'City Level 2' banner opens over the money, speed buttons and purple tip. Because the card is 94% opaque, the old tip's white text ('Place your buildings...') shows through behind the reward lines, so the player reads two layers of text at once. The saves dialog has the same translucency, with the road visible through it on saves@desktop.
findings.fix: Give .banner and .dialog a solid background:#fff. While the level banner is open, hide the tutorial card, since its tip belongs to the finished level. Below 720px, place the banner under the HUD rows (top:150px) so it doesn't cover the speed control.
findings.evidence: contrast.md level-up@phone: "+$8,000 road budget · 1 area unlock" p10 1.93:1 (declared 6.11); tip text under the banner p50 1.08:1. The banner [~55,52,280,172] overlaps the tutorial [192,44,190,98] and the speed group [80,45,106,24]. hud.css --card: rgba(255,255,255,0.94) is used for .banner and .dialog.

findings.title: Building-count badges are 10px and sit on top of the building icons
findings.detail: The small numbers on the building tools show how many of each building are left to place (for example 14 homes). They are 10px grey digits drawn directly over the coloured icons, so they blur into the green house and blue shop artwork.
findings.fix: Give the badge its own plate: .tool .count { font-size:11px; font-weight:600; color:#26282c; background:#fff; border:1px solid #c9cac3; border-radius:7px; padding:0 4px; top:-4px; right:-4px; line-height:13px }, so it sits on the corner instead of on the icon.
findings.evidence: contrast.md fresh-city@desktop: "14" 10px, p10 2.71:1; "1" 10px, p10 1.66:1 (size fail on all three badges). hud.css .tool .count { font-size:10px; color:#5d6168; position:absolute; top:1px; right:2px } with no backing.

findings.title: Building stock counts are 10 px superscripts, and used-up buildings just fade out
findings.detail: How many houses, shops and offices remain is exactly what the 'All buildings placed · 6 to go' goal depends on, but the count is a tiny 10 px grey number tucked against the icon. Once the shop and office are used up, their buttons just turn pale, with no '0' or reason, so they read as disabled for no clear cause.
findings.fix: Show the count as a 12 px+ number in a small solid badge on the button corner, and show '0' on exhausted buildings (with a 'none left' tooltip) instead of only fading the icon.
findings.evidence: city@desktop.dom.json: '6' [816,851,6,13] 10 px rgb(93,97,104). In fresh-city, '14', '1' and '1' are also 10 px (p10 2.71 and 1.66:1 over the icons). The 'Small Commercial' [827,849,38,38] and 'Small Office' [867,849,38,38] buttons have no count once used up.

findings.title: Cursor chips give cost, angle and length equal weight, so the price doesn't stand out
findings.detail: New idea (decision value first): the number that decides whether to commit the road is its cost, but the three chips are identical white boxes with 12 px regular text. '$937' reads no louder than '33.7°'. The player has to read all three to find the price.
findings.fix: Make the cost chip 600 weight (and red when it exceeds the budget). Merge angle and length into one quieter grey chip.

findings.title: Inspector rows wrap into two-line grey labels, and the filled 'Commercial' badge outweighs the building name
findings.detail: New idea (row integrity): each factor row should read as one line. The 11 px grey labels are squeezed into a ~103 px column, so 'Access to / workers/customers' and 'Access to input / resources' wrap and their values float mid-row. That makes the rows ragged next to the one-line 'Air pollution'. The filled blue 'Commercial' tag is the strongest mark in the panel, ahead of the name and the satisfaction verdict, and it is a pill badge, which the art direction avoids.
findings.fix: Narrow the bars (or drop them under the label) so labels stay on one line in the 264 px panel. Replace the blue badge with a small coloured square or text in the zone colour before 'Small Commercial', and keep the name as the strongest text.
findings.evidence: 'Access to workers/customers' box [1179,284,103,28] (2 lines), value '100%' at y 291. 'Access to input resources' [1179,316,81,28]. 'Commercial' white on rgb(47,134,224) [1185,238,65,14]. On phone the rows fit on one line ([19,613,156,14]).

findings.title: 'Air pollution: none' carries a red mark that reads as a warning
findings.detail: In the building inspector, a perfectly clean shop still shows a red sliver at the start of the Air pollution bar. Red elsewhere means a problem ('6 to go', 'Remove lights'), so a new player looks for a pollution issue that isn't there. Same on building-panel@phone.
findings.fix: Draw an empty grey bar when the value is none, and use red only when pollution actually lowers satisfaction.
findings.evidence: Row 'Air pollution ... none' [1179,348,242,14]. The bar starts with a red tick while the other two rows' bars are green at 100%. · building-panel@desktop: 'Air pollution' [1179,348,65,14], 'none' [1395,348,26,14], with a red sliver at the left end of the bar around x≈1313, y≈355. building-panel@phone shows the same red sliver at about (263,656).
alsoNoted: hud: Air pollution 'none' is drawn with a red bar stub

findings.title: 'Remove lights' (destructive) is the most prominent button in the junction panel
findings.detail: The red outlined 'Remove lights' is the only coloured control in the panel and sits bottom-right, where the primary action usually goes. '+ Add phase' is plain grey. The eye lands on the action that deletes the setup rather than the one that builds it.
findings.fix: Make 'Remove lights' a quiet text link (grey, red on hover) or move it under a divider at the bottom-left, and let '+ Add phase' carry the accent.
findings.evidence: 'Remove lights' text rgb(217,68,63) with red border [1319,436,102,26]. '+ Add phase' dark text with grey border [1179,436,92,26].

findings.title: Focus ring is a light blue that fails 3:1 and looks the same as the 'selected' style
findings.detail: Keyboard users (the game has shortcuts for every tool) get a 2px #45b0e5 outline as their focus mark. On the white cards it is faint, and it is the same colour as the border used for the selected tool, the selected speed and the active phase, so a focused control can't be told apart from a selected one. The level-up banner also opens without moving focus to Continue (level-up dom focused: null), while the saves dialog correctly focuses the name field.
findings.fix: Change the focus style to outline:2px solid #1677b3; outline-offset:2px (about 4.9:1 on white). Keep #45b0e5 for selected state only. When the level banner appears, call focus() on its Continue button.
findings.evidence: hud.css button:focus-visible, input:focus-visible { outline:2px solid var(--sel-line) } where --sel-line is #45b0e5, about 2.4:1 against #fff (non-text minimum is 3:1). The same #45b0e5 is the border of .tool.on, .btn.on, .seg-btn.on and .phase.on. saves@desktop shows the focused input [513,393,359,27] with this ring.
